Hi Samir / Ava —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps to keep momentum on the integration and address the infra/security questions your team raised: 

Recap (from our call):
- Goal: Run Redwood inference from FinPay workloads via private connectivity (VPC endpoints / IP allowlist) to avoid public internet egress and meet compliance requirements.
- Primary integration pieces: SDK auth, routing to dedicated/private model endpoints, structured output / tool-calling for reranker + embeddings pipeline, and networking (VPC endpoints, IP allowlists, egress, DNS, mTLS).

Open items we promised to follow up on:
1) IP allowlist ranges and sample firewall rules for your infra team.
2) Details on how mTLS is supported (termination at endpoint vs client-side certs) and recommended approach for Dedicated vs Private deployments.
3) DNS / split-horizon guidance so your services resolve control-plane vs private endpoints correctly.
4) SDK auth options: API key scopes, short-lived tokens, and Private deployment auth patterns (instance role / signed requests).
5) Example routing and embedding/ re-ranker flow (how to call embeddings, store vectors, and call reranker endpoint).

Attachments I've included: redwood_vpc_integration_guide.pdf (detailed steps + diagrams) and network_diagram.png (example topology). Marissa & Jonas are looped for the technical specifics — Marissa will send sample allowlist entries and SDK snippets; Jonas will provide firewall rule examples.

Proposed next steps:
- Can your infra/security folks review the attached guide and confirm whether PrivateLink (AWS) or IP allowlist + NAT is preferred?
- If okay, schedule a 60-min integration deep dive next week with your infra and our SEs.

Available windows: Tue/Wed morning PST or Thu afternoon PST.

Thanks — look forward to getting this scheduled.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Hi Samir — thanks for the notes. I've added details below and attached a short allowlist file (redwood_vpc_allowlist.txt) with CIDR blocks and FQDNs we commonly use. See inline answers: 

1) mTLS / TLS termination - For Redwood Hosted (public + PrivateLink): we support TLS to the endpoint and token-based auth (API key or short-lived tokens). If you use AWS PrivateLink, mutual TLS can be configured at the PrivateLink endpoint for extra assurance; however, the most common pattern is:
  - Use PrivateLink to keep traffic on the AWS network.
  - Use TLS + API keys scoped to the dedicated deployment.
  - Optionally enable client certs if your compliance team requires mTLS.

For Redwood Private (customer-managed, on-prem/VPC): we can support strict mTLS with customer-owned certs and HSM/KMS integration. Let us know if you want that option and we'll share the cert provisioning flow.

2) IP allowlist / VPC endpoints- If you prefer PrivateLink: create an interface endpoint in your VPC and route calls to the endpoint (no public IP egress).
- Fallback: allowlist our egress NAT ranges (see attached).
- Sample: allow outbound TCP 443 to the following FQDNs/IPs: api.redwood-inference.com, control.redwood-inference.com, s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (for plugin/artifact access).

3) DNS / split-horizon- We recommend split-horizon DNS so api.redwood-inference.com resolves to private IPs inside your VPC (PrivateLink) and to public IPs elsewhere. If you can provide the domain your DNS team uses for internal overrides, we can provide the private IPs to add.

4) SDK auth / routing- SDKs: set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your app environment or use our token exchange for short-lived creds. For Dedicated deployments we can scope keys to only route to your tenant's endpoints. For Private we support instance-role / signed request models if you prefer no static keys.

Example curl (embeddings):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \n    -d '\{"model":"redwood-embed-1","input":"..."\}'

Reranker flow (recommended):
- Step 1: Call embeddings endpoint to vectorize document corpus. Store vectors in your vector DB (we often see customers use Pinecone/Weaviate/FAISS).
- Step 2: At query time, call your vector DB for nearest neighbors, then call Redwood's reranker endpoint (a lightweight scoring endpoint) to get final ranking using the model and structured output.
- We can host the reranker route inside your Dedicated deployment so latency is minimized.

Attachments: redwood_vpc_allowlist.txt (sample CIDRs + FQDNs), redwood_vpc_integration_guide.pdf (step-by-step), network_diagram.png.

Next steps: please share a contact for your firewall/NOC team and preferred time for the integration deep dive. I'll also include a short code sample repo after this email.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi all — quick firewall snippet your infra team can paste: 

# Outbound (from FinPay VPC)
- Allow TCP 443 outbound to: api.redwood-inference.com (resolve to PrivateLink IPs)
- Allow TCP 443 outbound to control.redwood-inference.com (for control plane events)
- Allow outbound to AWS services: s3.*, ecr.*, sts.amazonaws.com (for artifact pulls/iam)

# CIDR samples (if you cannot use PrivateLink)
- 203.0.113.0/24
- 198.51.100.0/24

# Notes:
- If you use a NAT gateway, ensure DNS resolution preserves the PrivateLink hostnames (split-horizon).
- For mTLS: if you opt for client certs, your infra team will need to present certs during TLS handshake; we'll provide the CA chain and sample client certs for testing.

If you can confirm whether FinPay uses centralized NAT or per-subnet NAT instances I can tailor the rules further.

Jonas
